## dependency_form
- Three prerequisite sentences, each verbatim once on its blocked hub with only same-form restatements; none in a depended-on or any other document (scripted exact-string scan).
- Depended-on hubs (decision, close-out, protection) describe their own write in the waited-on state's words ("decides a price claim still pending … records on the decision", "close-out line is a removal line", "price protection line") and never mention the policy that waits on them.
- No tool name of another problem, no route, no chain, no ordered cross-problem steps, no cross-problem example/FAQ, no wrong-vs-right contrast in any document. The close-out reference factor's first tier ("Where the latest decision recorded on a price claim for the item … records the unit price the agreement sets") is the source ladder's own wording; it names no tool, policy or order and is a value rule, not a route.
- Titles general ("Reviewed Escalation Decisions on Pending Price Claims", "Close-Out of Discontinued Items", "Price Protection Lines for Substitutes of Discontinued Items", "Price Claims on Protected Substitute Lines", factor titles by evidence subject); the claim hub names the on_request policy's request type — not a mirror.
- Factor documents: none names another factor or a computation document; each places itself against a baseline quantity (reviewed escalation allowance, close-out price, protected price, unrounded claim amount); none states which tier customers fall on.
- Computation documents: generic combination sentences only (as task 0); no hint forms.
- Blind hop marks: all three hops state-derived; none pre-solved.
